hero.lead: A nation of 10.6 million with forest across two thirds of its land and two thirds of its power renewable, with public debt of 34.5% of GDP.

capital.heading: Forests, clean power and low debt, and incomes to match.

register.name: Kommuninvest social sustainability loans, 2025
register.detail: Kommuninvest · impact report for Social Bonds, 4 November 2026 · SEK 7bn disbursed at the end of 2025, up 56% · 34 projects in 24 municipalities · first Social Bond of SEK 3bn in April 2025
register.note: About 860,000 people are in the target groups of the projects
register.text: Loans from Kommuninvest, the funding agency of Swedish local government, for social investment projects reported under its Social Bonds. They finance housing and residential environments, safety and accessibility, and health, education, sports and culture, such as renovated residential areas, special housing, schools and preschools, which carry the shelter, education and health standards.

register.name: Kommuninvest green benchmark bond (US dollars, October 2029)
register.detail: Kommuninvest · priced 9 September 2026 · due 10 October 2029 · 25 bps over mid-swaps · about SEK 9.5bn · orders above US$2.5bn from over 50 investors
register.note: The first green transaction of the year in the US dollar market, Kommuninvest says
register.text: A green bond of Kommuninvest, the funding agency of Swedish municipalities and regions. Kommuninvest’s Green Loans finance municipal projects in renewable energy, energy efficiency, green buildings, sustainable transport and water and wastewater, which bear on the energy, water and shelter standards.

register.name: Three-year bond in euros (2.75%, June 2029)
register.detail: Swedish National Debt Office · sold 10 June 2026 · due 18 June 2029 · coupon 2.75% · yield 2.837% · price 99.753% · 5 bps below euro mid-swaps · about SEK 21.8bn
register.note: Bids of €8.2 billion from 81 investors; the currency risk is hedged with derivatives
register.text: A bond of the Kingdom of Sweden in euros, part of the Debt Office’s funding plan for central government borrowing. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Kommuninvest green benchmark bond (euros, February 2030)
register.detail: Kommuninvest · priced 19 May 2026 · due 20 February 2030 · 4 bps over mid-swaps · about SEK 13.6bn · orders above €2.5bn from over 60 investors
register.note: Investor interest followed the growing portfolio of green investment projects, Kommuninvest says
register.text: A green bond of Kommuninvest, the funding agency of Swedish municipalities and regions. Kommuninvest’s Green Loans finance municipal projects in renewable energy, energy efficiency, green buildings, sustainable transport and water and wastewater, which bear on the energy, water and shelter standards.

register.name: Kommuninvest Green Loans, 2025
register.detail: Kommuninvest · Green Bonds Impact Report 2025, 25 March 2026 · commitments SEK 134.2bn · SEK 99.6bn disbursed · 748 projects · green bonds outstanding SEK 84.2bn
register.note: Water and wastewater investments grew by SEK 3.3 billion in the year; 598,644 tonnes of CO₂ reduced or avoided each year
register.text: Green Loans from Kommuninvest to Swedish municipalities and regions for 748 investment projects, beside SEK 84.2 billion of its green bonds outstanding. The largest emission cuts come from renewable energy, energy efficiency, green buildings and sustainable transport, and water and wastewater lending is growing, which carries the energy, water and shelter standards.

register.name: Government bond SGB 1068 (2.75%, February 2037)
register.detail: Swedish National Debt Office · syndicated 11 March 2026 · due 9 February 2037 · coupon 2.75% · yield 2.855% · price 99.025%
register.note: Bids of SEK 50 billion, more than double the issue; 40 investors in the final bidding
register.text: A new nominal government bond of the Kingdom of Sweden, part of the Debt Office’s borrowing plan published in November 2025. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Sovereign green bond (0.125%, September 2030)
register.detail: Swedish National Debt Office · priced 1 September 2020 · settled 9 September 2020 · due 9 September 2030 · coupon 0.125% · reoffer yield 0.090% · orders above SEK 47bn
register.note: The first sovereign green bond of Sweden, under a framework the Government adopted in June 2020; an older instrument, due 2030
register.text: The first green bond of the Kingdom of Sweden, linked to central government spending on the protection of valuable natural environments, climate investments and railway maintenance. It is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · grants · Council approval 4 May 2022 · amended in 2023, 2024 and 2025 · third and fourth instalments authorised 21 September 2026 · fifth and last instalment authorised 5 October 2026
register.note: Five instalments of €3,445,666,208 in all (arithmetic); the Commission gives the value of the plan as €3.5bn, including the part financed with national resources
register.text: EU grants for Sweden’s reforms and investments, paid in five instalments against milestones and targets. They include €296 million for new rental homes with lower rents, €308 million to scale up university education, €196 million for vocational training, €452 million to train staff in elderly care and €811 million for local and regional climate investment, which carry the shelter, education, health and energy standards.

register.name: Drinking water, City of Stockholm (Stockholms Framtida Vatten)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · announced 31 August 2026 · 15 years · SEK 2bn · part of a programme of about SEK 5bn, due for completion in 2035
register.note: Reservoirs, transmission pipelines and treatment systems; complements the City’s financing in the bond market
register.text: An NIB loan to the City of Stockholm for its drinking water system: the renovation and expansion of water reservoirs, transmission pipelines and upgrades to treatment systems. It carries the water standard in the capital.

register.name: Electricity grid and water networks, Municipality of Borlänge
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · loan dated 20 April 2026 · 15 years · SEK 250M · on-lent to the municipal utility Borlänge Energi · €10.9M disbursed · financed from NIB Environmental Bond proceeds
register.note: Transmission capacity expected to rise by 23 MW; the water investments protect the local groundwater catchment
register.text: An NIB loan to the Municipality of Borlänge, on-lent to Borlänge Energi, to co-finance electricity grid infrastructure and drinking water and wastewater networks. It carries the energy and water standards.

register.name: Wastewater treatment and collection tunnel, City of Stockholm
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20240806 · signed 5 January 2026 · announced 26 March 2026 · €463.5M signed · long maturity to match completion in 2031
register.note: Around 26% of a SEK 19.5 billion investment, with a new tunnel to carry sewage from Bromma to Henriksdal
register.text: An EIB loan to the City of Stockholm to expand and modernise the Henriksdal wastewater treatment plant and build a new collection tunnel, to treat the city’s sewage, reduce overflows and protect the Baltic Sea. It carries the shelter standard, measured by safely managed sanitation, and the water standard.

register.name: University buildings in Solna, Gothenburg and Uppsala (Akademiska Hus)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · signed, announced 18 December 2025 · about €63.6M · borrower Akademiska Hus, owned by the Swedish state · total cost about SEK 1,400M
register.note: Each building moves up at least one energy class, several by up to three
register.text: An NIB loan to Akademiska Hus, the state-owned university property company, to refurbish education and research buildings in Solna, Gothenburg and Uppsala. It bears on the education standard at university level.

register.name: Energy-efficient rental housing and elderly care (Rikshem)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20250829 · signed 5 November 2026 · €100.1M signed of SEK 2,200M (€198M) proposed · total cost SEK 3,377M · about 70,000 m² of lettable area
register.note: New construction and renovation of energy-efficient homes and elderly care homes
register.text: An EIB loan to the housing company Rikshem for the new construction and renovation of rental housing and elderly care facilities in Sweden. It carries the shelter standard and, through elderly care, the health standard.

register.name: Energy-efficient schools and public buildings (Hemsö)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20250170 · signed 3 February 2026 · €200M in all: €135.4M for Sweden, €39M for Finland, €25.6M for Germany
register.note: Nine projects: four new schools, a health centre, an ice rink and a police headquarters, and the renovation of two schools
register.text: An EIB loan to Hemsö, a developer of social infrastructure, to build and renovate energy-efficient schools and other public buildings, with energy use more than 40% better than required. It carries the education standard and, through a health centre, the health standard.

register.name: Schools and judicial buildings (Hemsö)
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · signed, announced 28 January 2026 · 12 years · Sweden and Finland, split not stated
register.note: A new elementary school in Ljungskile doubles capacity to over 1,000 places
register.text: An NIB loan to Hemsö for buildings of the judicial system in northern Sweden and new schools in Sweden and Finland, among them an elementary school in Ljungskile. It carries the education standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 16.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: Matmissionen
items.text: Social supermarkets that Sweden’s City Missions run with the Willys chain of the food group Axfood, selling surplus food at greatly reduced prices to members on low incomes or benefits and offering work training to people far from the labour market, with 15 stores in operation in August 2025.

items.name: Fryshuset
items.text: A non-profit foundation, founded in 1984, that runs six schools in the Stockholm area with about 2,500 pupils, among them compulsory schools in Husby, Akalla and Hammarby Sjöstad, and meets on average 11,745 young people a month, financed by school funding, contracts and commercial activities as well as gifts and grants.

items.name: Yalla Trappan
items.text: A work-integration social enterprise in Malmö’s Rosengård, run as a non-profit with commercial activities, where women far from the labour market work in its sewing workshop, kitchen, lunch café, catering and cleaning; it employs 46 people on permanent contracts, and 65% of its turnover of SEK 26 million in 2025 came from sales.

items.name: Karins Döttrar
items.text: A textile cooperative in Gothenburg, part of the Vägen ut! cooperatives, that offers women and non-binary people far from the labour market work training, language training and creative work making small batches of textile products from reused materials, and received the Impact Stipendium in 2025.

items.name: Reningsborg
items.text: A Gothenburg organisation that gives people experiencing homelessness, mental ill-health or addiction work training in its own second-hand shops, bicycle workshops and dog day-care, under contracts with the Public Employment Service, the Social Insurance Agency, the City of Gothenburg and the Prison and Probation Service.
